text:
emily tran: hey team — baby arrived early and is in the NICU. my original 12-week parental leave ends next week. can i extend for the NICU stay? worried about pay, benefits, and my review window.
michelle (People Ops): first, so sorry — sending hugs. yes, we can extend leave for documented medical need (NICU). two paths: short-term disability (STD) if eligible, or unpaid medical extension. we'll walk you through both.
emily tran: thanks. what docs do you need and how fast does payroll need it?
lina (Benefits): we need hospital documentation confirming NICU admission + expected care dates. for STD file: physician's attestation + hospital discharge estimate. submit asap — payroll cutoff is Tue. STD can be retroactive to the day your leave began.
jordan (Payroll): payroll coding: if STD approved, code as "Short-Term Disability - Parental" (paid per STD rules). If unpaid extension, code "Medical Leave Extension - Unpaid". If you want to bump to paid using accrued PTO, mark that on the form. Submit before Tue 5pm to affect next cycle.
tara (Manager): Tara here — I will block you as "on leave" in org chart and pause any near-term review actions. Emily, we can postpone your review window 60 days automatically for documented medical leaves; tag me on the form and i'll route approval.
emily tran: do i need to worry about equity vesting or promotion timelines?
michelle (People Ops): equity vesting continues per grant agreements unless you elect to use unpaid leave that affects service time (rare). we can confirm specifics with Total Rewards. Promotions/benchmarks: Tara can request a formal deferral for review deadlines; won't count negatively.
legal (Legal): for international employees or visa holders: document medical leave and loop Legal for any visa/work-auth questions. Employment status remains active when leave is approved; travel during NICU stay may have visa/reentry implications.
lina (Benefits): COBRA/benefits: your active coverage continues while on paid STD; if you go unpaid >30 days we trigger benefits billing — we'll notify you and offer short-term continuation options.
emily tran: what's the hospital note look like? can someone paste a sample?
leave-bot: Sample hospital attestation (paste into form): ```Patient: [Child Name]\nHospital: [Hospital Name]\nAdmitting diagnosis: Prematurity / NICU admission\nAdmission date: 2026-03-20\nEstimated discharge: 2026-04-10 (subject to change)\nCertifying clinician: Dr. A. Rivera, Neonatology\nContact: 555-123-4567\n```
emily tran: if STD does not cover the full gap, can i use PTO for the rest?
jordan (Payroll): yes. hybrid coding allowed: STD covers eligible period, then "PTO" can top up paid time. if PTO used concurrently, specify on the form so we don't double-pay.
michelle (People Ops): timeline: 1) submit medical extension form + hospital attestation, 2) Benefits reviews STD eligibility (24-48h), 3) Payroll codes and any retro pay visible next cycle, 4) Manager confirms review deferral and backfill plan.
emily tran: how about backfill / handover — do i need to do anything while inpatient?
tara (Manager): don't worry about handover right now. i'll coordinate with the team to cover critical items and will set a brief async doc handoff — nothing live required from you until you're ready. we'll keep you looped via weekly update. :heart:
legal (Legal): quick note on documentation retention: we retain medical certs in HR file for audit; we redact sensitive clinical details.
emily tran: thank you everyone. i'll upload the attestation later today and tag Tara + Michelle. appreciate the quick responses. :pray:
